question: I’m a nurse reviewing our patient records and I need to find out how many patients fit the following criteria: their recovery status is unknown, they had an emergency room visit, and the vaccine was administered at a school clinic. These patients also have a recorded disability, and their vaccine was received on January 2, 2023. One of their reported symptoms is hypercalcaemia, and unfortunately, they died after vaccination. The symptom onset date was March 12, 2021, and the VAERS report was completed on May 19, 2023. They also had an office visit recorded and initially exhibited an imaging procedure artifact. The vaccine administration date was January 29, 2021. Their allergy history includes latex, hydrocodone, adhesive tape, propranolol, and gluten intolerance. Another symptom listed is decreased lipase. The detailed symptom narrative says: “I started feeling nausea a few weeks before the event and took ZOFRAN. On February 10, 2023, I began a double dose of lansoprazole. My symptoms included lack of appetite, stomach discomfort, a feeling of complete fullness, and I was unable to eat, only trying to keep fluids and basic nutrition. I tried to get an appointment with my gastroenterologist, but the first available was March 10, 2023. On February 15 and 16, 2023, I felt lightheaded and winded; I couldn’t tell if it was reflux or something else. On February 13 and again on February 17, 2023, I passed out; my husband caught me and called EMS. They came, and I regained consciousness right away. I was taken to the ER due to concerns of a heart attack or anxiety. I was released on February 17, 2023, around 5 PM. They told me the conditions were a perfect storm, describing a vasovagal episode, stress, and anxiety. I was advised to follow up with my primary care physician. On February 21, 2023, I saw my PCP, who coordinated with the gastroenterologist to schedule an endoscopy on March 2, 2023.
